title: [recoverability] Free text the SQL functions write into control records is masked by the store first (mission text, brief, report, notes, reasons, charter, summary; limits kept), and a source URL carrying credentials is refused by name
prompt:
Spawn, objective 171 [recoverability] (projects-47, 2026-11-14: the credential-cleanup line, 170's second half; rev-e; reviewer rev-g, then cc-astra): free text that the SQL functions write into control records is masked by the store first, and a source URL carrying credentials is refused by name.

R3 (rev-g's FIX F2 on R2; scenario only, code s171 4289e47b unchanged): 171.sh adds (5). A worker's report is checked end to end: a resident under a real `spawn loop`, on bb_engine's fake engine (j04's harness), writes .spawn/report.md holding the made-up token and a PGPASSWORD= value, and the stored report holds neither. report-unmasked now fails 171.sh.

R2 (rev-g's FIX F1 and note on R1; tests only, s171 4289e47b): the worker's report and the restart's byte limit are each held by a test of their own. Code is unchanged.

Independent of 170. It does not build on 170's code and applies alone on live main or on 170. 170 masks the records the Rust side builds and hands to SQL whole. 171 covers the records the SQL functions build themselves from their parameters, which 170 never sees.

Why. spawn_mission_add, spawn_task_assign, spawn_task_review, spawn_mission_pause, spawn_source_hold and the others build their control records in SQL from a command's arguments. A token pasted into a mission's text, a brief, a review note or a hold's reason is stored as written, folded into mission_missions.text, mission_tasks.brief and review_note, sent to agents and shown on the page. On live (the lead's scan, 11-14): 0 hits so far, in source.held 207, source.push_requested 148 and task.reviewed 68 records among others.

Read: crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs (the store methods named below); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (each function's record and its length checks: hold and pause reasons 500 chars, push reason 2000 chars, restart and reassign reasons 2000 bytes); crates/spawn-core/src/redact.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/sources.rs (MissionSource::parse).

What changes (the candidate, 171-fleet.diff, no protected path):
- spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs adds masked(text) = spawn_core::redact::redact(text), and masked_strings(value), which masks every string of a JSON value. They are applied to the free-text parameters before SQL sees them:
  - mission_add text, mission_close summary;
  - task_assign and objective_assign brief;
  - task_reported report;
  - task_review note;
  - task_report_unfinished note and markers (its digest is the caller's hash, kept);
  - task_fork_failed error;
  - task_restart and task_reassign reason;
  - resident_propose charter;
  - mission_pause reason, source_hold reason, source_push_request reason;
  - task_reissue attempts.
  The SQL compares what it is given, so its own comparisons stay consistent: the brief's md5 index and the interventions join see the same masked text on both sides. The Rust readers compare stored text only with stored text (scorecard history's brief).
- masked_within(text, limit, chars) keeps a limited reason within its limit when it was within it (masking can lengthen a short secret), cut at a char boundary. It applies to the hold and pause reasons (500 chars), the push reason (2000 chars) and the restart and reassign reasons (2000 bytes). Text already over its limit is not cut, so the store refuses it as before.
- spawn-cli/src/sources.rs MissionSource::parse (mission add and configure, push, refresh) refuses an https:// source with any userinfo (`user:password@`, or a token as the user) and an ssh:// source with a password. The error: "a source URL carries credentials (its userinfo, before the host's @): give git its credentials through a credential helper or an ssh key, not in the URL (<the source with its userinfo removed>)". (R4, cc-astra A76) A source refusal does not repeat a credential, whatever its form: the userinfo is taken out structurally (sources::without_userinfo: in any text that is not a path, everything before its last @ becomes "<userinfo removed>", keeping only a real scheme at the very start (letters, then letters, digits, +, - or .); R5, rev-g F1: neither a later :// nor where the first / falls is trusted), not by matching what a credential looks like, so an opaque token as the user or an all-digit password goes too; the malformed-source refusal shows the source the same way; the length refusal shows no text at all ("a source is at most N bytes, not M"). (R5, rev-g F1) An https:// or ssh:// source whose port is not digits from 1 to 65535 is refused (sources::port_is_digits): `https://u:abc/<secret>@host/r.git` read as host u, port abc, which no git can fetch, and was stored. (R6, rev-g F2) That refusal comes before any other and shows the scheme alone: a password written where the port goes (`https://oauth2:<token>/r.git`, the host forgotten; or all digits, longer than a port) has no @ to cut at. (R6, rev-g) A refused text that is neither an absolute path nor a URL with a real leading scheme is never a source and is not shown at all: "(not shown: N bytes)" ("oauth2:<token>" or a token pasted alone). (R7, rev-g F3) A refusal shows the text only for an absolute path or a URL that begins exactly https:// or ssh:// (those have passed the port check); under any other scheme, or the same one in other letters (http://, HTTPS://, ftp://, git://), a password where the port goes has no @ to cut at, so the text is not shown. (R8, cc-astra A83) After four rounds each found one more shape (a token as the user, a password where the port goes, under another scheme, before a second colon), no URL-shaped or non-plain-path input is echoed by parser refusals (the plain-path exception kept): every refusal gives a fixed explanation, the scheme from a known list (https, ssh, http, git, ftp, file; else another scheme or no scheme) and the length (sources::described); only an absolute path with no ':' and no '@' is shown. without_userinfo is gone. The port is what follows the first colon of an unbracketed host, so `https://user:<secret>:443/r.git` (port "<secret>:443") is refused, not accepted and stored; ports 1 to 65535 in digits and bracketed IPv6 hosts stay accepted. That rule and the credential rule are spawn-cli's; the schema's spawn_source_allowed stays the rule of shape. An ssh user alone (ssh://git@host/…), an @ in the path, and scp-style sources (git@host:path) stay accepted. (R9, rev-g's R8 review, owner part only) 171.sh (4) also holds, black box, what the unit test alone held: an ssh:// URL with a password (opaque or all digits) is refused, a text port after a bracketed IPv6 host is refused, port 0 is refused, and a path holding an @ that is refused for a control character is not shown. This closes 170's named residual for new sources. Live sources are local paths.

What stays as it is: the schema and every function, record shapes, the identifiers, names, digests and keys passed beside the text, and 170's scope.

Residuals, named: scripts/rsi/nightly.sh writes its alerts by psql, outside both masks. Its text is generated; it is scoped after 171 (the lead, 11-14). Past records are not rewritten.

Tests:
- spawn-postgres missions::tests::text_for_a_control_record_is_masked_within_its_limit: a token becomes [redacted]; a 500-char reason of é ending in " PWD=x" stays at 500 chars; a 2000-byte reason stays within 2000 bytes; text already over is not cut; nested JSON strings are masked.
- spawn-postgres/tests/text_masked.rs, through the real store:
  - a mission's text, a task's brief and report and a review's note are masked in each record and in mission_missions.text, mission_tasks.brief and review_note, and the task still ends in revise;
  - a hold's and a pause's 500-char reason ending in a short secret is taken, stored within 500 chars and masked;
  - a charter and a closing summary are masked.
- (R2) spawn-cli deliver::tests::a_reports_credentials_are_stored_masked: a worker's .spawn/report.md holding a token and a PGPASSWORD= value, taken by collect_reports through the real store (PostgresStore). task.reported.report and mission_tasks.report hold [redacted] and neither value. A report has no command: the deliver loop records it, reading the workspace's .spawn/report.md once the worker's facts say it is due. This test drives that route (collect_reports) on the real store, and 171.sh (5) (R3) drives it through a real `spawn loop`.
- (R2) spawn-postgres tests/text_masked.rs a_restart_reason_at_its_byte_limit_stays_within_it: a restart's 2000-byte reason (997 é and " PWD=x") is taken once masked and stored within 2000 bytes. A count in chars at that call site would let it grow past the store's byte limit.
- 171.sh samples the routes (a mission's text, a brief, a pause's reason, a source URL, and (R3) a worker's report through the loop). The tests above cover each parameter's route.
- spawn-cli sources::tests::a_source_url_carrying_credentials_is_refused_by_name: four URLs refused by name without repeating the token or password; ssh with a user only, @ in a path, and scp-style accepted.
- (R4) spawn-cli sources::tests::no_refusal_repeats_a_credential_in_any_form: an opaque token as the user, an all-digit password, a credential in an overlength source, in a malformed (ftp://) source and in a source with no scheme, and (R5) one before a :// that is no scheme and three behind a / before the @ (a malformed URL, another scheme, a port that is not digits): each refused, and no refusal holds the credential; (R6) a password where the port goes (https://user:<s>/r.git, ssh://git@host:<s>/r, after a user and host, all digits): refused without repeating it; ports 1 to 65535 in digits (and IPv6 hosts) stay accepted, any other port (0, 65536, letters, empty) is refused.

Files: crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs (+125 −16 with its unit test), crates/spawn-postgres/tests/text_masked.rs (+187, new), crates/spawn-cli/src/sources.rs (+269 −5 with its tests), crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs (+42, its test). Owner: rsi/scenarios/171.sh. Size: +623 −21 with R8 (+615 −21 at R7, +601 −21 at R6, +555 −22 at R5, +485 −19 at R4 +406 −16 at R2, +335 −16 at R1). The lead kept the userinfo rule in, 11-14.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/171.sh, black box, on its own database and scratch HOME.
(1) `spawn mission add --text "<a GitHub token behind Bearer, a PGPASSWORD= value>" --source <dir>` exits 0. Neither the mission.added record's text nor the mission's text holds them; each holds [redacted].
(2) `spawn task assign --brief "<the same>"`: the task.assigned record's brief and the task's brief hold neither value.
(3) `spawn mission pause --id N --reason <500 chars ending " PWD=x">` exits 0, and the stored reason is at most 500 chars without "PWD=x".
(4) `spawn mission add --source https://user:<token>@host/r.git` exits non-zero, says the URL "carries credentials" without repeating the token, and no mission names that source. (R4) Nor does any refusal repeat an opaque token as the user, an all-digit password, a credential in an overlength URL, in a malformed (ftp://) source, or in a source with no scheme (u:<digits>@host), nor (R5) one before a :// that is no scheme (u:<s>@host/x://y) or behind a / before the @ (https://u:abc/<s>@host/r b.git, ftp://u:abc/<s>@host/r.git, and https://u:abc/<s>@host/r.git, refused for its port), nor (R6) a password where the port goes (https://user:<s>/r.git, ssh://git@host:<s>/r, https://user:<digits>/r.git), nor (R6) a user and token or a token pasted alone (oauth2:<s>, <s>), nor (R7) a password where the port goes under http://, HTTPS://, Https://, SSH://, ftp:// or git://, nor one behind a / with no port in a malformed https:// URL, nor (R8) one before a second colon in the authority (https://user:<s>:443/r b.git, ssh://git@host:<s>:22/r b.git, https://user:<s>:443/r.git refused, ssh://git@host:<digits>:22/r), nor one in a path refused for a control character. (R9) Nor is an ssh:// URL with a password taken (ssh://git:<s>@host/r.git, ssh://deploy:<digits>@host/r.git), nor a text port after a bracketed IPv6 host (https://[2001:db8::1]:<s>/r.git), nor port 0; and a path holding an @ that is refused for a control character (/srv/<s>@host\x01) is not shown.
(5) (R3) A resident (`spawn resident propose`/`approve`, its own mission) is given a task (`spawn task assign --kind resident --brief "BB:WORK …"`) and started under a real `spawn loop`, with the fake engine of scripts/blackbox/assertions.sh's bb_engine, its own tmux socket and no model judge. Its turn writes .spawn/report.md with the token and a PGPASSWORD= value in it. Once the task is reported (within 90 s), neither the task.reported record's report nor mission_tasks.report holds either value, and each holds [redacted].
The base (main 6f8ceb8c, which this change is rebased onto) exits 1 at (1) to (5).

Proof: 171-proof.txt (rev-e-96); R9's, 171-r9-proof.txt (rev-g).

Verified by: after the landing and deploy, the lead's value scan of new control records' strings (names and counts only) reads 0. A `spawn mission add` with a credential-carrying URL is refused by name.
